Use this reusable template to write and share your knit stranded colorwork yoke sweater patterns in Markdown. Fill in the bracketed sections with your pattern details. This template works for seamless top-down pullovers with a stranded colorwork yoke, optional waist shaping, and matching colorwork bands on the body and sleeves.

**Related guides:** [Garment measurements](/reference/garment-measurements/), [Repeats and sizing](/style guide/sizing/), [Gauge](/style guide/gauge/), [Abbreviations](/style guide/abbreviations/)

### Colorwork Notes

- **Color dominance:** When working stranded colorwork, carry the contrast color to the left and the main color to the right. The strand held farthest left will float above the other, creating larger, more prominent stitches.
- **Float tension:** Carry floats loosely across the back of the work. Stretch the stitches on the right needle to their full width before working the next color to avoid puckering.
- **Jogless stripes:** When changing colors, [describe jogless method used, e.g., lift the first st of the new color up one round].
- **Chart repeats:** The yoke chart is worked [N] times per round. Mark your chart for your size before beginning.

### Pattern Notes

- Construction: Seamless top-down. Work collar, then colorwork yoke, short row shaping, separate body and sleeves, waist shaping, colorwork band, sleeves with matching colorwork band.
- Collar: [Rolled or Ribbed — worked first on smaller needles]
- Colorwork: Yoke chart is worked in stranded colorwork. All other sections in Stockinette stitch unless noted.
- Short rows: Used after yoke to raise back neckline, and optionally after body separation for additional lower back length.
- Waist shaping: Optional. Work decreases at waist, increases at hips for a fitted silhouette.
- Bands: Colorwork band + ribbing at body hem and sleeve cuffs.
- Stitch counts are given in order: A (B, C, D)(E, F, G, H).

## Pattern Instructions

### Collar

With MC and smaller 16 in / 40 cm circular needle, loosely CO [N] sts. Place marker and join for working in the round.

**Option 1: Rolled Collar**

```plaintext
Knit [N] rnds even.
Next Rnd: *K[N], Inv-L; repeat from * to end — [N] sts increased.
Knit 2 rnds even.
```

**Option 2: Ribbed Collar**

```plaintext
Rnd 1: *K1, p1; repeat from * to end.
Repeat this rnd until ribbing measures [N] in / cm.
```

**Option 3: Double-Folded Collar**

```plaintext
Rnd 1: *K1, p1; repeat from * to end.
Repeat this rnd for [N/2] rnds.
Next Rnd: Purl all stitches (fold line).
Repeat Rnd 1 for [N/2] rnds.
```

Fold collar in half along purl round so cast-on edge sits inside your circular needle. For each live stitch, pick up the corresponding cast-on stitch, place it on the left needle, and work them together as k2tog.

**Finish Collar (All Versions)**

Switch to larger needles for small-circumference knitting.

```plaintext
Next Rnd: [Knit increase round to reach yoke starting count.] — [N] sts now on needles.
```

### Set Up Yoke (Larger Sizes Only)

If your stitch count does not evenly divide by the chart repeat, work M1L increases as follows to reach the correct count:

[N] sts now on needles.

### Yoke

Switch to larger circular needle (longer cable as needed). Join CC1 and work Rounds 1-[N] of Yoke Chart.

**Chart instructions:**

```plaintext
Work Yoke Chart rounds in stranded colorwork. Chart is repeated [N] times per round.
Read chart from right to left on all rounds.
Hold CC strand to the left of MC for optimal color dominance.
```

**Chart increases:** This chart uses yarnover increases (YO) blended into the colorwork. Grey squares represent YO stitches — work them through the back loop on the following round to close the hole.

**Jogless colorwork:** To avoid a visible jog at the BOR in the colorwork pattern, slip the first stitch of the round purlwise with yarn held in back on [Rounds N, N, N...].

After completing chart, continue in Stockinette stitch with MC until yoke measures [N] in / cm from first round of colorwork.

**[N] total sts now on needles.**

### Short Row Shaping (Back Neck)

Short rows raise the back neckline relative to the front for a better fit. Use your preferred short row method.

Place markers for sleeve separation. Make each marker distinct:

```plaintext
K[N] back sts, pm A, K[N] sleeve sts, pm B, K[N] front sts, pm C, K[N] sleeve sts.
```

```plaintext
Short Row 1 (RS): Knit across back to marker A, sm, knit across sleeve to marker B, sm, k[N], turn.
Short Row 2 (WS): Purl to marker B, sm, purl to marker A, sm, purl to BOR, sm, purl to marker C, sm, p[N], turn.
[Continue short rows, working progressively farther from markers, until N sts remain unworked at each side.]
Final row: Knit to BOR, closing short row gaps using your preferred method.
```

### Separate Body and Sleeves

Knit across back of sweater to marker A. Remove marker.

```plaintext
Transfer next [N] sleeve sts onto stitch holder or waste yarn for first sleeve.
CO [N] underarm sts with backward loop method. Place side marker.
CO [N] more underarm sts with backward loop method.
Remove marker B. Knit across front of sweater to marker C. Remove marker.
Transfer next [N] sleeve sts onto stitch holder or waste yarn for second sleeve.
Remove BOR marker.
CO [N] underarm sts with backward loop method. Place new BOR marker.
CO [N] more underarm sts with backward loop method.
```

[N] total sts now on needles.

### Body Short Row Shaping (Optional)

Short rows add length to the lower back for a better fit.

```plaintext
Knit 2 rnds even.
Short Row 1 (RS): Knit across back to side marker, sm, k[N], turn.
Short Row 2 (WS): Purl to side marker, sm, purl to BOR, sm, p[N], turn.
[Continue until N sts remain unworked at each side.]
Final row: Knit to side marker, closing gaps. Sm, knit across front to BOR, closing gaps.
```

### Body

Work even in Stockinette stitch until front of body measures [N] in / cm from underarm cast-on.

**Waist Shaping (Optional):**

Omit for a straight silhouette. Work for a fitted silhouette.

**Decrease section:**

```plaintext
Decrease Rnd: K[N], k2tog, knit to [N] sts before marker, ssk, k[N], sm, k[N], k2tog, knit to last [N] sts, ssk, k[N].
[N] sts decreased.
Repeat Decrease Rnd every [N]th rnd [N] more times.
[N] sts now on needles.
```

Work even until front of body measures [N] in / cm from underarm.

**Increase section:**

```plaintext
Increase Rnd: K[N], Inv-R, knit to [N] sts before marker, Inv-L, k[N], sm, k[N], Inv-R, knit to last [N] sts, Inv-L, k[N].
[N] sts increased.
Repeat Increase Rnd every [N]th rnd [N] more times.
[N] sts now on needles.
```

Knit even until front of body measures [N] in / cm from underarm (or [N] in / cm less than desired final body length).

### Body Band

Knit Rounds 1-[N] of Band Chart. Chart is repeated [N] times per round.

```plaintext
Knit 2 rnds even with MC.
```

Switch to smaller 24 in / 60 cm circular needle.

```plaintext
Next Rnd: *K1, p1; repeat from * to end.
Repeat this rnd until ribbing measures [N] in / cm.
BO all sts in rib pattern.
```

**Tubular cast-off (optional, recommended):**

```plaintext
Set-up Rnd 1: *K1, sl 1 purlwise WYIF; repeat from * to end.
Set-up Rnd 2: *Sl 1 purlwise WYIB, p1; repeat from * to end.
Cast off all stitches using sewn tubular bind-off method.
```

### Sleeves (Both Alike)

Transfer [N] sleeve sts from stitch holder or waste yarn to spare needle.

With RS facing, join MC at the beginning of the underarm cast-on edge on the body. With larger small-circumference needles:

```plaintext
Pick up and knit [N] sts from CO edge. Place BOR marker.
Pick up and knit [N] more sts from CO edge.
Pick up and knit 2 sts in the corner between CO and sleeve.
Knit across sleeve sts from spare needle.
Pick up and knit 2 sts in the gap between sleeve sts and armhole.
Knit to BOR.
[N] sts now on needles.
```

Knit even in Stockinette stitch until sleeve measures [N] in / cm from underarm.

**Sleeve shaping:**

```plaintext
Decrease Rnd: K[N], k2tog, knit to last [N] sts, ssk, k[N].
[N] sts decreased.
Repeat Decrease Rnd every [N]th rnd [N] more times.
[N] sts now on needles.
```

Work even until sleeve measures [N] in / cm from underarm (or [N] in / cm less than desired final sleeve length).

### Sleeve Band

Knit Rounds 1-[N] of Band Chart. Chart is repeated [N] times per round.

```plaintext
Knit 1 rnd even with MC.
```

Decrease round (if needed to reach ribbing stitch count):

```plaintext
*K[N], k2tog; repeat from * to end — [N] sts decreased.
[N] sts now on needles.
```

Switch to smaller small-circumference needles.

```plaintext
Next Rnd: *K1, p1; repeat from * to end.
Repeat this rnd until ribbing measures [N] in / cm.
BO all sts in rib pattern.
```

**Tubular cast-off (optional, recommended):**

```plaintext
Set-up Rnd 1: *K1, sl 1 purlwise WYIF; repeat from * to end.
Set-up Rnd 2: *Sl 1 purlwise WYIB, p1; repeat from * to end.
Cast off all stitches using sewn tubular bind-off method.
```
